text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Ten companies from Northern Ireland, on their first ever trade mission from the Industrial Development Board of Northern Ireland, are due to come to Vietnam next weekend to explore business opportunities.

-- Vietnam and Italy signed an agreement at avoiding double income tax during a visit by Italian Deputy Foreign Minister Patrizia Toi. Discussions were also held on a $60 milliion credit from the Italian government.
-- United Nations Resident Coordinator in Hanoi Roy Morey told a new conference that if Vietnam wants to catch up in the next century it must take some basic policy decisions.

-- Vietnam officially promulgated the amended Foreign Investment Law and the Law on issuing and implementing legal documents, which were endorsed by the National Assembly and approved by President Le Duc Anh.
-- Singaporean Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Tony Tan held talks with chairman of Ho Chi Minh city's Municipal committee Vo Viet Thanh on opportunities for further cooperation.
